title: Metal vs fiber post: where the stress goes
topic: Stiff metal posts load the post–dentin interface, fiber posts load cervical dentin; ferrule and remaining dentin matter most.

claims.claim: Load case 1: 100 N at 45° on the palatal surface (model setting)
claims.source: Nokar S et al., J Dent (Tehran) 2018;15:69-78 (PMID 29971124; full text: 100 N at 45° on the lingual surface); Yang B et al., Int Dent J 2025;75:100918 (PMID 40684680; 100 N at 45° on the palatal surface); Asmussen E et al., J Prosthet Dent 2005;94:321-9 (PMID 16198168; 100 N at 45°, axisymmetric model)

claims.claim: Elastic modulus (GPa, approx.): dentin 18–25, fiber post 20–40 (axial), gold ~90, titanium ~110, steel/zirconia ~200; metal/zirconia ≈ 4–11× dentin
claims.source: Kinney JH et al., Crit Rev Oral Biol Med 2003;14:13-29 (PMID 12764017; dentin 20–25 GPa); Nokar S et al., J Dent (Tehran) 2018;15:69-78 (PMID 29971124; Table 1: dentin 18.6, quartz/carbon/glass fiber 18.7/21/40, gold 88, Ti 112, steel/zirconia 200 GPa); Badami V et al., Cureus 2022;14:e29753 (PMID 36324349; glass fiber ~40, Ti 115, steel/Ni-Cr/zirconia ~200 GPa)

claims.claim: Metal post: peak dentin von Mises stress along the post–dentin interface
claims.source: Pegoretti A et al., Biomaterials 2002;23:2667-82 (PMID 12059016); Adanir N, Belli S, Eur J Dent 2007;1:67-71 (PMID 19212479)

claims.claim: Fiber post: peak in cervical dentin, like natural teeth
claims.source: Pegoretti A et al., Biomaterials 2002;23:2667-82 (PMID 12059016); Adanir N, Belli S, Eur J Dent 2007;1:67-71 (PMID 19212479); Nokar S et al., J Dent (Tehran) 2018;15:69-78 (PMID 29971124; fiber-post peak at the cervical root). Note: Nokar does not support the metal-interface pattern (its metal peaks were also cervical, and cast posts gave the lowest stress)

claims.claim: Stress maps are schematic (not a solve), relative scale, contrast exaggerated; real FEA differences are modest and studies disagree
claims.source: Toy model / schematic: analytic fields shaped after Pegoretti 2002, Adanir & Belli 2007 and Nokar 2018; disagreement: Asmussen E et al., J Prosthet Dent 2005;94:321-9 (PMID 16198168), Nokar 2018 (PMID 29971124)

claims.claim: Lab overload: metal post → root fracture below the crest, often non-restorable; fiber post → core/cervical failure above the crest, often restorable (crack paths illustrative)
claims.source: Akkayan B, Gülmez T, J Prosthet Dent 2002;87:431-7 (PMID 12011860); Fokkinga WA et al., Int J Prosthodont 2004;17:476-82 (PMID 15382786)

claims.claim: Cast posts often fail at higher loads, but less favourably
claims.source: Fokkinga WA et al., Int J Prosthodont 2004;17:476-82 (PMID 15382786)

claims.claim: Caveat: clinical studies show similar root-fracture rates for metal and fiber posts
claims.source: Figueiredo FE et al., J Endod 2015;41:309-16 (PMID 25459568); Martins MD et al., J Dent 2021;112:103750 (PMID 34274439)

claims.claim: A post retains the core; it doesn't reinforce the root
claims.source: Guzy GE, Nicholls JI, J Prosthet Dent 1979;42:39-44 (PMID 379307; no significant reinforcement from a post in vitro); Naumann M et al., J Endod 2018;44:212-219 (PMID 29229457; 7 of 8 clinical studies show no post effect); Schwartz RS, Robbins JW, J Endod 2004;30:289-301 (PMID 15107639; narrative review)

claims.claim: Ferrule + remaining dentin matter most; with a 1.5–2 mm ferrule, post type matters less; clinical evidence limited
claims.source: Juloski J et al., J Endod 2012;38:11-9 (PMID 22152612); Naumann M et al., J Endod 2018;44:212-219 (PMID 29229457); Martins MD et al., J Dent 2021;112:103750 (PMID 34274439)

caption:
Metal vs fiber post: where does the stress go?

Many FEA models: stiff metal posts (≈4–11× dentin's modulus) concentrate dentin stress along the post–dentin interface; fiber posts load cervical dentin, like a natural tooth.
Lab overload: metal → more root fractures; fiber → more restorable failures. Clinically, root-fracture rates are similar.
A post retains the core; it doesn't reinforce the root. Ferrule + remaining dentin matter most.

Refs: Kinney 2003, Crit Rev Oral Biol Med; Nokar 2018, J Dent (Tehran); Pegoretti 2002, Biomaterials; Adanir & Belli 2007, Eur J Dent; Asmussen 2005, J Prosthet Dent; Akkayan & Gülmez 2002, J Prosthet Dent; Fokkinga 2004, Int J Prosthodont; Figueiredo 2015, J Endod; Martins 2021, J Dent; Guzy & Nicholls 1979, J Prosthet Dent; Naumann 2018, J Endod; Juloski 2012, J Endod
Animation is schematic, not an FEA solve.
